analysis: Washington is favored by 3-3.5 across books (down a touch from the -4.5 high earlier in the week), but the sim now has the Giants favored outright (58.7% win, WAS covers only 30.5% of sim trials) after Stefon Diggs (hamstring) was ruled out and Terry McLaurin remains limited with his own hamstring. New York's own injuries (Golston, Pinnock) are rotational-depth losses on defense, not offensive starters, so they are noted but not priced into the Giants own scoring.

Important correction: the market-side line move toward Washington is news-driven, not unexplained sharp money -- Jayden Daniels is expected back at QB after missing two games with a dislocated elbow (reported Oct 7), and Washington's backup options (Mariota hurt, rookie Kaliakmanis 15/33 in relief) are weak enough that his return alone moved the number. 93% of handle is still on New York and the line has moved toward Washington anyway (apply_market_signal.py flags this as a genuine reverse line move toward the home favorite), but given the Daniels-return explanation this reads as the market correctly pricing a real QB upgrade, not necessarily sharp money disagreeing with our injury-driven Giants lean. We keep the Giants lean on model+injury grounds while flagging that the line move itself has an honest news explanation, which tempers how much weight the RLM tag alone should carry here.
